children: The Commodity Futures Trading Commission allowed the expansion of crypto and prediction market trading platforms by exempting some software providers from registration requirements, the agency said Thursday.

Specifically, the CFTC's Market Participants Division issued a no-action letter that states that under certain specified conditions, it will not recommend enforcement action against certain passive software providers that facilitate trading but never take custody of a user's assets.

"This applies solely in relation to their provision and marketing of software to facilitate trading by the provider’s users with registered futures commission merchants, introducing brokers, and designated contract markets," the CFTC said in a statement.

Until recently, companies that solicited or accepted trade orders, sent them to futures commission merchants, and received fees or commissions would be required to register as brokers. In March, though, the CFTC issued a no-action letter in response to a request from Phantom Technologies, a developer of self-custodial crypto-asset wallet software. Phantom has partnered with Kalshi
to allow predictions trading through its more than 20M crypto wallet holders, Bloomberg News reported.

title: CFTC allows expansion of predictions, crypto trading through online platforms
